- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 18-day average (e.g., < 10% below), consider mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates in early periods (days 1–7) when sentiment is positive — increase forecast slightly for first 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model tends to lag — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in the 10–15 day window to catch reversal.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — model often overcorrects; use 3–5 day sentiment average for smoothing.
